title: Debts commonly not discharged in bankruptcy
facts: Federal bankruptcy law excludes or limits discharge for various categories of debt.
Examples can include certain taxes, domestic support obligations, many government fines or penalties, and debts arising from specified misconduct, depending on statutory requirements.
Debts for money obtained by fraud and certain other categories may require a creditor to successfully bring an adversary proceeding for a nondischargeability determination.
A debtor should not assume a debt is discharged solely because it was listed in the bankruptcy schedules.
